newsitem.title: USA: U.S. suspends aid to Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. suspends aid to Cambodia.

text.p: The United States announced on Thursday it was suspending aid to Cambodia for 30 days in response to the seizure of power by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the aid cutoff -- part of an international effort to put pressure on Hun Sen -- was "a clear signal to Hun Sen and his associates that the U.S. will not be conducting business as usual with those individuals."

With the United States preparing for talks here on Friday with Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, Burns spelled out Washington's messages for the embattled leader, including a renewed warning that efforts to join forces with the reviled Khmer Rouge guerrilla group were unacceptable.
"I think that we simply would not ... support in any way, shape or form any senior member of the Khmer Rouge playing a role in the political life of Cambodia," the spokesman said.

He also crticized Hun Sen's threat to put Ranariddh on trial if he returned to Cambodia, saying: "That's not appropriate. He (Ranariddh) should be allowed to return freely and participate ... in political life there."

After mulling the issue for several days, "the United States has decided to suspend our aid programmes to Cambodia for 30 days while we conduct an intensive review of those programmes," Burns told a regular news briefing. The review would include consultation with other countries.

After 30 days, and depending on the circumstances in the country, "we would anticipate resumption of those programmes which do provide humanitarian people-to-people support in the area of basic human needs," he said.
But he added the United States would not resume "those portions of our aid programme that in some way, directly or indirectly, support the government of Cambodia."
Burns could not give details of how much aid would be cut. The United States allocated $35 million in aid to the Southeast Asian state for fiscal 1997 ending on Oct. 1.

"We hope very much that Hun Sen will reconsider his actions of going it alone, of rupturing the Paris peace accords and breaking the coalition government that had been in place for the last four years," the spokesman said.
He endorsed the decision of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), the region's main collective institution, to postpone plans to bring Cambodia into the organisation this year.

He also said the United States fully supported ASEAN's decision to send the foreign ministers of Indonesia, the Philippines and Malaysia to Beijing to consult with Cambodia's King Sihanouk because "we believe (he) has an important role to play in this conflict." Sihanouk is receiving medical care.

Ranariddh, in New York on Thursday, was to meet on Friday in Washington with Undersecretary of State Thomas Pickering, who is standing in for Secretary of State Madeleine Albright while she is in Europe.

Ranariddh had been attempting to make alliances with Khmer Rouge forces when Hun Sen took over the government. Burns said this was a major mistake and he would be told "any cooperation with the Khmer Rouge is certainly not acceptable to the United States." The guerrilla group was blamed for more than one million deaths during its rule of Cambodia from 1975-79.

The United States also would make clear that it believed Hun Sen's offensive against Ranariddh was unacceptable behaviour and that it hoped both prime ministers would "find a way to restore a functioning coalition in Cambodia."

That last message was delivered to Hun Sen on Wednesday by a State Department official through Cambodia's ambassador to Washington, a member of Hun Sen's party. U.S. Ambassador to Cambodia Ken Quinn has attempted to see Hun Sen but so far has been refused, Burns said.

Burns said about 400 Americans left Cambodia in the last few days after fighting erupted in Phnom Penh over the weekend and between 900 and 1,000 remained. The embassy staff of 61 is being cut to 20 and Burns said those leaving would begin to do so in the next few days.
